cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body:
The issuer describes itself as 'an integrated gold and silver platform in India serving businesses and consumers, with a presence across 24 states, as of March 31, 2026', whose 'operations span across multiple segments of the gold and silver value chain including procurement and refining, bullion trading, digital gold offerings, jewellery manufacturing, international sales and facilitating gold-backed financial services.'

BACKWARD INTEGRATION (upstream). Procurement runs through four disclosed channels: refined gold and silver bought from Indian and international banks; doré bars imported and refined in-house, which the RHP quantifies as carrying import duties 'lower ... by 0.65% as compared to directly importing refined gold'; scrap gold and silver bought from individuals, jewellers and at jewellery auctions 'at reduced rates'; and refined metal imported through the IIBX via the GIFT City subsidiary Augmont IFSC Private Limited, where the issuer 'execute[s] transactions directly as a trading member', saving 'expenses associated with brokerage and commission', and where 'the gold is procured from sources such as LBMA-accredited refiners or UAE Good Delivery-accredited refiners'. The issuer then owns the refining step itself, through two units (Rudrapur 144 MTPA and Mumbai 140 MTPA as of March 31, 2026) with in-house NABL/ISO-IEC-17025:2017-accredited assaying laboratories and BIS hallmarking licences, certified under India Good Delivery standards and authorised to deliver refined bullion on BSE- and MCX-operated commodity exchanges.

MANUFACTURING. A jewellery manufacturing unit at Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur, Rajasthan (13.80 MTPA installed capacity as of March 31, 2026) converts metal into gold jewellery articles, primarily chains, for the international sales business.

FORWARD INTEGRATION (downstream). The issuer owns and operates both of its distribution platforms — 'Augmont SPOT' for enterprise customers (operational since 2012, 5,223 registered members) and 'Augmont Gold For All' for consumers (launched Fiscal 2021) — and owns the price-discovery layer on the enterprise side ('our pricing engine monitors these inputs through a combination of our in-house technology, AI powered tools and human oversight ... live tracking, predictive analysis and efficient hedging strategies'; 'we do not charge users of our platform any brokerage or terminal fees and we include our margins in the prices that are quoted on our platform'). Physical last-mile is partly owned and partly outsourced: of 20 spot delivery centres across 13 states, nine are operated directly and 11 through franchisees, with delivery 'typically fulfilled within two working days'.

WHERE INTEGRATION STOPS — THIRD-PARTY AND RELATED-PARTY DEPENDENCE. The consumer physical network is NOT owned: all 106 Gold-For-All centres are 'operated by Finkurve', a Group Company, and the issuer 'maintain[s] an asset light structure at these centers as they do not carry physical inventory'. Gold lending is not undertaken by the issuer at all — under a service level agreement dated June 1, 2024 (effective July 1, 2024) it only 'provide[s] technology, marketing and brand support through our platform for gold loans provided by' Finkurve. Consumer reach otherwise depends on third parties: 'over 218 partners such as Gullak, and Candere' for order placement, Kalyan Jewellers and CaratLane for physical redemption of digital gold, 3,700 Muthoot Fincorp branches for investment jewellery (a Technopak-sourced figure), an unnamed NBFC's stores, 705 independent financial agents, and third-party payment gateways for collections. The issuer states the synergy rationale itself: 'the gold and silver that we procure for selling on our 'Augmont SPOT' platform, helps us with our raw material requirements for manufacturing jewellery as well as for the other products and services that we provide through our consumer-focused business, thereby serving multiple business verticals', alongside centralised 'finance, information technology, strategy and procurement' functions.

STATED EXPANSION OF THE CHAIN. ₹ 4,650.00 million of the Net Proceeds is proposed to be used 'towards funding future working capital requirements towards procurement of raw material, maintenance of inventory and funding advance margin requirements for procurement purposes'; 15 new spot delivery centres are planned in Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities by Fiscal 2029; the issuer intends to fund 'minimum order quantity commitments under long-term supply arrangements our Company may enter with miners, in Fiscals 2027, 2028 and 2029'; and it 'also propose[s] to expand our refining op' — the routed extract is cut off mid-sentence at that point, so the refining-expansion plan itself is NOT in the provided extract.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body:
AFFIRMATIVE NIL. The RHP states, under its own heading 'SEASONALITY OF BUSINESS' in MD&A, verbatim and in full: 'Our business is not seasonal in nature.' No qualification, quarter-weighting or festive-demand percentage is printed by the issuer.

COUNTERVAILING LANGUAGE ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME RHP (recorded, not reconciled): the Business chapter says the procurement footprint 'enables us to benefit from favourable pricing terms and sell our products throughout the year'; the Strategies section states the inventory-funding object will enable the Company to 'manage customer orders during peak demand periods'; and MD&A notes 'the number of orders that our customers place with us may differ from quarter to quarter, our results of operations have fluctuated in the past and we expect this trend to continue in the future' — attributed there to customer demand variation rather than to seasonality. Festive/gifting demand is discussed only in the commissioned Technopak industry chapter ('conversion of digital gold into physical jewellery, often around festive or gifting occasions'), which is not the issuer's own disclosure.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- We primarily conduct our business through our two online platforms ‘Augmont SPOT’ and ‘Augmont Gold For All’, which are owned and operated by us, and any significant disruptions in our information technology systems or breaches of data security could adversely affect our business and reputation.
- Our ‘Augmont SPOT’ platform enables businesses such as jewellers, bullion dealers and manufacturers with valid GST registrations to purchase gold and silver bars online with assured physical delivery.
- Any technical failure, settlement delay, charge-back fraud, phishing attack, SIM-swap fraud, or compromise of communications channels could disrupt collections, erode customer trust and result in financial losses.
- As we expand our customer base, transaction volumes, and product offerings, we may need to make frequent upgrades to our software architecture, data processing systems, cybersecurity protocols, and user interfaces.
- Any failure to effectively manage these upgrades, whether due to delays in implementation, software bugs, system incompatibilities, or inadequate testing, could result in service disruptions, transaction errors, or degraded user experience.
- Such issues may lead to customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, and potential financial or legal liabilities.
- The occurrence of such events may adversely affect our business, results of operations and cash flows and our insurance coverage may not be adequate to cover all the costs related to such attacks or disruptions resulting from such events.
- Conversely, during periods of falling prices, customers may delay purchases in anticipation of further declines, which can lead to reduced transaction volumes on our platforms and lower sales across our product lines.
